comments.body:
Phase 1 confirmed RCA (rebar-debug).

Proven root cause — tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:77-106 uses aggregate nested-pytest wall time as a functional oracle for the five-second repo-isolation watchdog. The outer subprocess timeout=12 at line 97 covers nested pytest startup, the intentional five-second blocked-Git watchdog, pytest session-finish/unconfigure, and runner scheduling. It therefore leaves only about seven seconds for unrelated overhead and turns a correct inner TimeoutExpired into failure on a loaded runner. The elapsed < 10 assertion at lines 103-106 is a second instance of the same defect: an otherwise functionally correct completion between 10 and 12 seconds is rejected.

Organic evidence — Gerrit 1869 run 32187810048/job 95875806054 failed only this macOS/Python 3.13 test at 12.04 seconds, after captured stderr already showed the intended inner git status --porcelain TimeoutExpired after five seconds. The sibling head test passed at 8.74 seconds and 13,880 other tests passed. Three concurrent macOS runs of unchanged code passed this same test at 7.64, 8.03, and 9.18 seconds; local macOS runs were 6.27-6.52 seconds.

Discriminating runtime proof — temporary instrumentation, removed before this comment, recorded the inner timeout, direct shim PID liveness, pytest_unconfigure boundaries, and nested completion while varying only teardown delay / the two aggregate timing knobs:
- delay=7, outer cap=12: OUTER_TIMEOUT at 12.008 seconds after INNER_TIMEOUT and UNCONFIGURE_START; blocked shim already dead.
- same delay=7, cap=30: COMPLETED functionally at 12.883 seconds, nonzero result with TimeoutExpired output, shim count 2, blocked shim dead.
- delay=5, cap=30 with elapsed<10 enforced: functional result at 11.030 seconds rejected only by ELAPSED_ASSERTION.
- identical delay=5 without elapsed assertion: COMPLETED functionally at 10.992 seconds.
This rules out failure to reach the second probe, failure of the five-second watchdog, a live-child/descriptor reap hang, and generic runner infrastructure. Runner load is the trigger that expands overhead; the changeable defect is the test's tight aggregate wall-clock oracle.

Defect legitimacy — defect. scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py:4-9 and :18-23 plus signed story faintish-bumbling-tadpole require structural/counting proof or a generous hang guard whose ceiling dwarfs expected time. The introducing callous-amused-hart report explicitly accepted the 12-second ceiling only because it should not determine functional success; this CI failure disproves that premise.

Caller-dependency gate — expected post-fix behavior is that shim count, nonzero nested result, and explicit TimeoutExpired output determine watchdog success, with only a genuinely generous outer stuck-process fail-safe. The helper has only the status/sessionfinish and head/autouse tests at lines 149 and 156; neither depends on the tight aggregate deadlines. No behavioral dependency blocks repair.

comments.body:
Final rebar-debug report.

Problem — the nested repo-isolation guard self-test could fail on a loaded macOS runner after the intended five-second Git watchdog had already fired.

Proven root cause — tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py coupled functional success to aggregate nested-pytest wall time twice: timeout=12 covered startup, the intentional five-second block, teardown/unconfigure, and scheduling; elapsed < 10 independently rejected correct completions. The inner tests/_isolation.py watchdog was working.

Proof — controlled runtime instrumentation showed delay=7/cap=12 timing out at 12.008s after INNER_TIMEOUT and UNCONFIGURE_START with the shim dead, while the identical cap=30 run completed at 12.883s with returncode nonzero, explicit TimeoutExpired output, and shim count 2. Delay=5/cap=30 completed near 11s and was rejected only by elapsed < 10. This ruled out watchdog failure, failure to reach the second probe, child reaping, and generic infrastructure.

Test — tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_deadline_heldout.py freezes the contract with a deterministic wall-clock fake: both normal 6s and overhead-expanded 13s completed results must be accepted, and the outer stuck-process fail-safe must be at least 30s. It was observed RED before repair, was hidden from the independent fixer, and is GREEN afterward. Reintroducing the exact timeout=12 plus elapsed < 10 defect returned both cases to RED; restoring the fix returned them to GREEN. The assertion was refined under the test-modification guard from exactly 30 to at least 30, re-proven RED without the fix, then GREEN with it.

Fix — tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py removes the aggregate elapsed measurement/assertion and raises only the outer stuck-process fail-safe from 12s to 30s. Structural success checks remain: the shim must be invoked twice, the nested process must be nonzero, and each caller still asserts explicit TimeoutExpired output.

Scope and safety — caller sweep found only the status/session-finish and head/autouse tests; neither depends on tight aggregate timing. The fix restores the original watchdog contract, adds no dependency, creates no new capability, and weakens no structural assertion. Focused file: 14 passed. Full non-integration/non-external make test: passed. make lint, make typecheck, wall-clock policy scan, and git diff --check: passed.

Siblings — construct sweep covered upper-bound wall-clock assertions and nested pytest subprocess deadlines. scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py reports clean. The only other shared nested-pytest harness, tests/_store_isolation.py, already uses a generous 90s fail-safe and has no aggregate elapsed oracle. Parity census: status and head both call the repaired shared helper; no CLI/MCP/library/automation/dual-direction product surfaces exist for this test-only harness. No sibling ticket required.

Residual risk and prevention — none observed beyond the fixed coupled deadline. The wall-clock assertion lint prevents recurrence of the elapsed-oracle half of the class; the held-out contract prevents regression of both deadline facets.

Replication — both original real blocking-Git nested-pytest scenarios pass after repair, with explicit TimeoutExpired behavior preserved; the full gating suite also passes.

## Context / Problem
Gerrit change 1869 patch set 1 (revision dcb219a7408e2ebeb68d3a17c97df4907b28ba2d) failed its sole macOS/Python 3.13 job in GitHub Actions run 32187810048. The failed test was tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py::test_session_finish_fails_explicitly_when_porcelain_times_out: its nested pytest subprocess exceeded the test harness's 12-second outer deadline even though captured stderr showed the intended internal git status --porcelain watchdog raising subprocess.TimeoutExpired after 5 seconds. The rest of the run passed (13,880 passed, 65 skipped); Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 all passed.

This ticket is intentionally separate from change 1869. The observed 5-second internal watchdog plus 12-second outer deadline is only a lead: investigate dynamically whether macOS teardown/scheduling overhead, product liveness, or unrelated runner infrastructure explains the failure.

## Plan
- Reproduce the real nested-pytest harness under controlled scheduling/teardown delays and capture the runtime path from the five-second Git watchdog through pytest session-finish cleanup.
- Generate and run falsifiable experiments that distinguish harness-budget exhaustion from a product watchdog failure and from unrelated runner infrastructure.
- After a proven RCA, encode the final observable timeout contract with a held-out RED oracle, repair via an independent fixer, then prove GREEN, exact-defect mutation RED, and original-report replication.
- Sweep sibling nested-process deadline tests for the same budget-coupling pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Runtime evidence proves a specific, changeable root cause and rules out product-watchdog and unrelated-infrastructure alternatives.
- [x] A final-form held-out regression test is observed RED before repair and GREEN afterward.
- [x] Reintroducing the exact defect returns the oracle to RED, then restoring the repair returns it to GREEN.
- [x] The original nested-pytest blocking-Git scenario completes reliably with the intended explicit watchdog failure under controlled macOS-equivalent teardown overhead.
- [x] Relevant focused tests plus lint and typecheck pass.
- [x] Sibling timing-contract occurrences are swept and every confirmed sibling is fixed or ticketed.

## Expected file impact
- tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py
